title: KV cache (quantized decode): avoid redundant scale/zero-point conversions in decode loop
author: Grace Kim
release_notes: - Runtime: quantized decode path avoids redundant KV-cache quant param conversions (scale/zero-point), improving TPOT and tail latency on decode-heavy workloads.
description:
Context: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint, we found unnecessary overhead in the quantized decode loop caused by repeatedly converting KV-cache quantization parameters (scale/zero-point) into the per-step kernel param format. The conversion itself is small, but it was happening on every decode step across layers, and showed up as measurable CPU-side overhead + extra device param traffic under higher concurrency.

What changed: This PR caches the derived QuantKVParams (the packed scales/zero-points + layout metadata used by the decode kernels) per (layer, kv-cache page) and reuses it across decode steps until the underlying cache block changes. The cache is invalidated when: (a) we advance to a new KV cache block/page, (b) quant mode changes, or (c) we detect a different quantization profile ID for the model.

Implementation details: The previous flow rebuilt per-layer quant params inside the decode loop by (1) reading scale/zero-point buffers, (2) converting to the packed dtype expected by the kernel launch, and (3) performing a small amount of layout bookkeeping. We now build these params once when a KV cache block is materialized for decode, store them in the per-sequence decode context, and pass stable pointers/handles to the kernel launcher. For safety, we keep the old code path as a fallback behind an internal flag (runtime.quant_kvparams_cache=0) for quick rollback.

Why this is safe: This is a pure refactor of how we prepare kernel parameters. The underlying scales/zero-points are unchanged. We add assertions to ensure the cached params are only reused when the KV cache block generation matches the expected one. If any mismatch is detected, we invalidate and rebuild.

Perf results (perf-lab):
- H100, INT8 quantized decode-heavy workload (short prefill, long decode, streaming on): TPOT improved ~2.8% median; p95 end-to-end latency improved ~1.6% at concurrency=32.
- A100, same workload: TPOT improved ~1.9% median; p95 improved ~0.8%.
- Prefill-heavy workloads: within noise (<0.5%) as expected.

Testing:
- Unit tests: added coverage for cache invalidation across kv-block rollovers and for mixed quant profiles.
- Correctness: ran existing INT8/FP8 drift checks locally against FP16 baseline on the standard short prompt set (see ENG-24810 notes). No changes observed beyond existing tolerances.
- Perf: benchmark-lab smoke run on A100 + H100 with the quant-perf config.

Rollout plan:
- Land in main behind default-enabled caching (runtime.quant_kvparams_cache=1). If perf-canary shows instability or unexpected correctness issues, we can disable via config and/or revert cleanly (isolated commit).

Follow-ups:
- If we’re happy with results after canary, we can remove the legacy path and simplify param preparation. Also worth checking if similar caching applies to the FP8 attention path’s auxiliary params (tracked in ENG-24810 working doc).
commits: runtime/kvcache: introduce QuantKVParams cache + invalidation hooks
runtime/decode: reuse cached packed quant params for quantized decode kernels
tests: add kvparams cache invalidation test cases (block rollover, quant profile change)
config: add runtime.quant_kvparams_cache flag (default on) + logging for cache hit rate
docs/internal: note new flag + perf rationale in quant perf sprint notes
conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (review): Can you clarify the invalidation conditions? I want to be sure we don’t accidentally reuse params across cache block reuse / eviction.

Grace Kim (author): Yep. The cache key is (layer_id, kv_block_id, kv_block_generation). We bump generation on reuse/eviction. Decode context stores the last-seen tuple; any mismatch triggers rebuild. Added assertions + a unit test that simulates block rollover.

Noah Patel (review): Perf numbers look good. Two asks: (1) please add lightweight counters for cache hit/miss so we can confirm behavior in perf-canary, and (2) can we ensure we’re not allocating per-step?

Grace Kim (author): Added hit/miss counters under existing perf event plumbing (guarded behind perf logging). Also switched the packed buffer storage to reuse a preallocated per-seq scratch arena; no per-step heap allocs.

Sofia Ivanova (review): Any scheduler interaction? We’ve been chasing tail latency in mixed prompt lengths and want to ensure this doesn’t increase per-request lock contention.

Grace Kim (author): This reduces work in the hot loop; we’re not adding locks. Cache is per-sequence decode context; no shared structures. Also added a small span annotation so we can see kvparams_build time separately if needed.

Julian Moore (review): Minor: can we rename quant_kvparams_cache to quant_kv_params_cache for consistency?

Grace Kim (author): Done.

CI notes: Initial run had a single flaky GPU test timeout (runtime_gpu_e2e_decode_smoke) on H100 runner; rerun passed. Merged via squash after approvals.
